emergency.title: Emergency help

injured: Call 112 or 108 now. Say where you are and how many people are hurt.
Make the scene safe: hazard lights on, warn traffic. Don't put yourself in danger.
Do not move an injured person unless there is fire or another immediate danger.
Check if they are breathing. If not, and you are trained, start CPR.
Press firmly on heavy bleeding with a clean cloth.
Keep them warm and talk to them calmly until help arrives.
Do not remove a motorcyclist's helmet.
vehicles: Turn on hazard lights and move to a safe place off the road.
Check everyone for injuries — some appear later. Call 112 if in doubt.
Take photos of the vehicles, number plates and the scene.
Exchange names, phone numbers and insurance details.
Report the accident to the police (100) if there is a dispute or damage to property.
unsure: If anyone could be hurt, call 112 now — it's better to be safe.
Keep yourself safe: stay off the carriageway and warn oncoming traffic.
Do not give an injured person food or water.
Stay with them until help arrives.

privacy_body: CityPulse helps citizens report road hazards. We collect only what that needs: your email and name (to sign you in), the photos you take, and the location of each hazard.
Publicly we show a cropped photo of the hazard, its location, its status and how many people reported it. We never show who reported it.
Your full photos are visible only to you and to city officers using CityPulse, so they can assess the hazard. Photo metadata (camera, phone GPS history) is removed when you upload.
We don't sell data and we don't use advertising trackers. Location is used only when you report or ask to see hazards near you.
You can delete your account at any time in Settings. Your reports stay on the map without any link to you.
Questions or requests: contact the CityPulse team through the address on the project's website.
terms_body: Report only real hazards that you have seen yourself, with your own photos.
Don't upload photos that focus on people, number plates or private property.
CityPulse is a citizen tool, not a government service. Sending a complaint to your city is your choice, and the city decides how to respond.
In an emergency always call 112. The first-aid guidance in CityPulse is general information, not medical advice.
Moderators may remove reports that are false, abusive or duplicates, and suspend accounts that misuse the service.
